engineering analysis below was prepared, sealed, and signed by Tom Green, P.E., the Intervenors’

                                                    Preface
This Preface is a personal introduction to this Brief, which is drafted by a
Professional Engineer.
I am not an attorney. I am unskilled in the legal vernacular and protocols.
Kindly extend your deference and utmost forbearance: this Brief is “my
ﬁrst rodeo” in an unfamiliar proceeding.
I am a Professional Engineer (PE). I perform many facets of professional
engineering. This Brief is consistent with my experienced reporting
regarding forensics and expert witnessing. It is not in the customary legal
format, but is nonetheless valid and appropriate information.
I present this Brief in response to my statutorily.entrusted.duty.to.project.
the.health?.safety?.property?.and.welfare.of.the.public. This duty was
borne out of an unspeakable 1937 New London School tragedy wherein
about 300 students and faculty died, another 300 were injured, all due to
the School Board’s decision to accept a known risk to save $300 per
month.
It is all too often that those accepting the known risks are the least likely
to be affected by the outcome.
Not unlike many others, I am but one guy. I have but a small time to do
what a team of people would need months, if not years, to do.
Unlike many others in this proceeding, I am not paid. Indeed, these
proceedings extract, immensely, both time and ﬁnances from my “day
job,” my small producer ranching operations, and my family joy and
obligations. As the saying goes, “walk a mile in my shoes.”




     Initial Brief of Intervenor the Thomas F. and Heidi A. Green Living Trust and Dos Brothers LLC Page 4 of 74
 My duty is unlike any other duty of any other professional, including
medical and legal and even government duty borne out of oaths. It is
more comprehensive. It is enforced. To me, it is sacred.
And, yet, to my knowledge, my Direct Testimony and this Brief are the
only engineering documents in the evidentiary record. There are several
direct and rebuttal testimonies wherein a PE introduces, presents, and
“sponsors” the testimony, but such.is.not.the.same as signing and sealing
a document as the responsible charge Engineer of Record (EOR). Those
other Engineers have not accepted the personal accountability as the
EOR, and hence their PE credentials are, I believe, inescapably diluted.
The result is that professional accountability would appear to be absent
for anything in the Permian Basin Reliability Plan (PBRP) or in its
proposed implementation in these Dockets 59182 and 59475.
Accordingly, that means that the largest transmission grid project in the
history of Texas has no professional accountability in which the public
can rely. Instead, the supposed accountability rests somewhere in
agencies/entities who have reportedly done engineering studies which I
have been unable to ﬁnd in the record.
I am often reminded that others’ words are often better than our own, and
when old, others’ words are best. Winston’s Churchill’s words on inaction
and consequences are a notable example.

“move the needle” to any noticeable degree. The die seems to have been
cast.
This Brief may not matter. It may not be heard. But that doesn’t mean it
should not be said.
Throughout this Brief, relevant and legitimate questions are being asked
and answers based on facts are being given. The words are not the
answers: words.are.always.drowned.out.by.decisions.and.actions¡
All.the.players.are.Executive.Branch¡.The PUC makes the rules, the SOAH
administers the rules in a quasi-judicial form, and then the PUC makes all
the ﬁnal judgments. It decides: accept, deny, or change however it elects.
Historically, those judgments and decisions consistently, near
universally, favor the industries (e.g., transmission companies) which the
PUC is supposed to regulate… for the protection of Texans. From the
public’s perspective, the system is woefully awry.
I do not come to this testimony either voluntarily or as an adversary to
any party. I come because I have been thrust into a battle in which the
law a PE serves compels him to engage… despite the near zero
resources now available, especially after the great Freeze, after the
Flood, and the beginning of the New World Screwworm battle. I
recognize the unfortunate reality that the “system” pits parties in
opposition. There are much better and more productive approaches than
excluding the public in the planning and later involving the public in only a
last step façade in which it hopes it will dissuade the already vested
planners. If the process is ﬂawed, the results are as well.

     Initial Brief of Intervenor the Thomas F. and Heidi A. Green Living Trust and Dos Brothers LLC Page 6 of 74
 Doing anything otherwise would not just be complacent, it would be
complicit. And with legitimate public issues surrounding the PBRP and
the ensuing CCNs, a complicit acceptance of the issues would not only
be wrong morally, it would be professionally suspect.
The PE’s role is not about winning. It is about doing.the.right.thing by
Texans.
The ultimate question is whether or not the primary objective to do the
right thing will be achieved, given the monumental disparity of resources
of the applicants compared to the intervenors, and given the history of
close ongoing and lasting relations between the applicants and the PUC.
We will see what the parties’ priorities are not by what words are spoken,
but by the decisions made.
Respectfully submitted,




Tom Green, P.E.

public’s health, safety, property, and welfare. There exist material or
even critical issues that are fully worthy of first-time examination or re-
examination.

   hyper-fast changes, including betterment opportunities, have
